macro: US equity futures are rallying Monday morning with S&P up 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 329 points or 110 basis points, and Russell 2000 up 47 basis points. Asian markets closed broadly higher led by Korea KOSPI up 1.65% and Hong Kong Hang Seng up 1.18%, while major Eurozone indices gained 85 to 120 basis points with strength in industrials, basic resources, tech, and banks. The primary driver behind Monday's strength appears to be optimism surrounding the UN General Assembly in New York this week, despite a weekend full of negative headlines including escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Ukraine's largest drone strike on Russia.
rates_fed: Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. The market is pricing in approximately 33 basis points of rate hikes over the Fed's final two meetings of the year, with roughly 50/50 odds of an increase at the October 28th meeting, and an additional 35 basis points of hikes priced in for 2027. Fed officials remain hawkish — Kansas City Fed President Schmid warned Friday that elevated inflation is being driven by more than just oil, and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari echoed those sentiments Sunday, saying inflation is reaching all corners of the US economy.
market_outlook: Adam's lean is cautiously mixed with a conditional bull bias — the key catalyst to watch today and this week is diplomatic progress at the UN General Assembly, specifically any signal of a Trump-Iran meeting or ceasefire movement that could trigger a meaningful drop in oil prices. If oil cracks lower, it unlocks a cascade of bullish macro effects including lower yields, reduced inflation, and improved consumer confidence, but the geopolitical backdrop remains fragile enough that a diplomatic disappointment could reverse today's gains quickly.
bull_case: The UN General Assembly running September 22 through 28 brings together leaders from Iran and key Middle East nations, creating a genuine window for diplomatic progress that could ease the Iran war premium baked into oil prices. Trump called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday and said he would be open to meeting Iran's president, suggesting a de-escalation path exists. Even a modest improvement in Middle East tensions would likely trigger an outsized drop in Brent crude, which at roughly $102 per barrel is already down on the week, potentially unleashing lower yields, better margins, and improved consumer confidence simultaneously. The Trump-Xi summit on Thursday September 24th also offers a near-term positive catalyst with modest tariff reductions possible on roughly $30 billion in goods.
bear_case: Nearly all the weekend news flow was net negative — Houthis dramatically escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia including targeting Riyadh's airport fuel depot, Ukraine launched its largest drone strike on Russia hitting oil refinery infrastructure, and Iran warned of a fierce response to any resumed US military action. The AI complex faces fresh headwinds after the Friday close brought a delayed Anthropic IPO, underwhelming Anthropic 2027 ARR projections, OpenAI's expected negative free cash flow of approximately $280 billion from 2026 to 2030, and Oracle data center debt issues in New Mexico. Oil tanker costs are surging, motor oil is being rationed by US retailers, and the global refining capacity shock from the Russia-Ukraine conflict has not been priced in by corporate earnings yet — demand destruction looks increasingly inevitable as energy price spikes work through the system.

Good morning. Here is your Monday September 21st morning game plan.

The macro picture this morning is all about diplomatic optimism overriding a weekend packed with bad news. US equity futures are rallying — S&P up 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 110 basis points, and small caps up 47 basis points. Asia closed broadly higher, with Korea up 1.65% and Hong Kong up over 1%. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points, with strength in industrials, banks, and tech. The driver here is this week's UN General Assembly in New York, and the hope that some diplomatic progress can be made on the Iran conflict. Trump reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night, and said he's open to meeting Iran's president, who is expected to be in New York. That is the market's green light this morning.

Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. But do not mistake this for a dovish Fed — Kansas City's Schmid and Minneapolis's Kashkari both made hawkish remarks over the weekend, warning that inflation is broad-based and not just an oil story. The market is pricing in 33 basis points of additional rate hikes over the final two Fed meetings of the year, with roughly even odds of a hike on October 28th.

On the company side, Novo Nordisk is underperforming in Europe after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to provide specific financial targets. Oracle is under pressure after a negative report on debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center — efforts to offload those loans have, quote, hit a wall. Disney's parks business is bucking the industry trend, outperforming peers by leaning into price promotions and package deals. The Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery deal is in advanced settlement talks with California regulators, though not all state attorneys general are on board, keeping the outcome murky. Nscale, the London-based neocloud company, filed its S1 Friday and plans to list on the NYSE — but the IPO timing could not be worse given the weekend's wave of negative AI headlines including Anthropic's delayed IPO and OpenAI's disclosed negative free cash flow of approximately $280 billion expected through 2030.

The Trump-Xi summit Thursday is also worth watching — modest tariff reductions on roughly $30 billion in goods are possible, and China eliminating tariffs on American LNG is reportedly under discussion.

For the directional read: the bull case is entirely dependent on oil. If Middle East diplomacy at the UN General Assembly produces even a small signal of de-escalation, Brent, currently around $102, could drop hard and fast, unleashing lower yields, better margins, and improved consumer sentiment all at once. The bear case is that the weekend's news — escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Ukraine's largest drone strike of the war on Russian refineries, Iran threatening fierce retaliation — is simply being papered over by hope. If diplomacy disappoints, this gap up has no legs. Stay close to oil headlines this week. That is the trade.
